DriftSense

A wafer-inspection microscope loses track of where it is. DriftSense finds a reference pattern inside the SEM frame under unknown 8–12× zoom and ±5° rotation, or reports that it isn't there.

my role
team lead · team of 4
stack
Python · PyTorch · OpenCV
when
sep 2026

$ cat problem.md

This is Applied Materials' Navigation-Error Recovery problem, Phase 2. Given a high-resolution reference patch and a low-resolution SEM search frame of a repeating semiconductor layout, locate the patch and report its position, rotation and scale, or report that it is not there. The zoom is unknown, between 8× and 12×, and the rotation is unknown within ±5°. About 20% of pairs contain no true instance.

The layout repeats, so a patch correlates well at many positions and local appearance alone cannot identify the site. The pipeline keeps the top few pose hypotheses from a coarse scale sweep, verifies each at full resolution with ZNCC, and keeps the best one.

$ cat limits.md

  • An earlier 81.45 / 81.93 result was withdrawn after a generator defect was found: a severity pinned to one value produced pairs at severity 0.0. It is not reported here.
  • The organisers' blind set is 200 pairs and is not reproduced here, so the F1 margin may not carry over.
  • Periodic layouts produce plausible wrong-scale and wrong-rotation matches. Sub-pixel refinement cannot recover a pair whose candidates never include the correct pose.
  • Some confidently wrong predictions score above the threshold, and no confidence cut catches all of them.
  • CAD-to-SEM registration assumes a whole-canvas search design file. Without it, the fallback scored 45.32 / 85 on the harsh tier, against 85.00 with it.
  • Runtime rows are local emulations of the 4-core, 8 GB reference box, not measurements on it.
